title: AI Engineer
description:
Legal AI is only as good as the knowledge behind it. At Lefebvre Sdu, we’ve been building that knowledge for 200 years. Day in, day out. Law by law. Word by word. Other legal AI tools run on our data and software. As the Dutch heart of Lefebvre Group, the European leader in legal and tax knowledge, we’re also developing our own platform: GenIA-L, where lawyers and tax professionals don’t just get an answer, but an answer they’re willing to put their name to. More than 75,000 professionals use it every day, accounting for over €100 million ARR across Europe. We’re looking for a Medior AI Engineer to help shape how the intelligent core of that platform evolves.

HOW YOU'LL MOVE US FORWARD 

GenIA-L is a research platform for legal professionals. A user asks a question. The platform searches our trusted sources and turns them into a useful answer. It does this with agents: specialised AI components that each handle part of the question and work together. In the legal domain, an answer can't just sound fluent. It has to be correct, and you must be able to see which source it comes from. This is not a pilot project: the platform runs in production and is used heavily every day.

As a medior, your focus is on building. You work independently, on challenges that come from customers and on challenges we spot ourselves. You break down a legal process, translate it into a technical process and work out how to best connect the pieces. Stuck on something? You say so, and your colleagues think along with you.

You build and improve the agents of GenIA-L and the way they work together.

You build and maintain our knowledge packages: for each legal article, an expert-validated set of commentary, case law, parliamentary history and practical interpretation. You also work on the pipelines that create these packages and keep them up to date.

You make quality measurable. With evaluation sets, observability and metrics, you show that answers, source attribution and reliability really improve. Not by gut feeling, but with evidence.

You build features for customers, such as analysing their own documents and new ways to search case law.

You work directly with editors and subject-matter experts, and check with them which parts of a legal question really matter.

You come up with and test ideas to make the product sharper or faster, and alternate AI experiments with back-end development.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 

You have a realistic view of LLMs. You see what they can do, but you also know their weak spots. You enjoy following new AI developments, but you don't just follow the herd: you stay critical. You think in a structured way and can break a complex problem into smaller pieces. You work independently, take initiative when things are unclear and are eager to learn fast. And you enjoy working with lawyers and editors, because they know what a good answer looks like.

- You have several years of experience in software or ML engineering. Depth in recent projects counts for more than years.

- You have good knowledge of Python and experience with relevant machine learning libraries.

- You have helped build an LLM application that runs in production. Not just prototypes, notebooks or courses.

- You have hands-on experience with agent frameworks such as LangGraph and LangChain, tool calling, MCP or comparable orchestration. Our entire product is built around this. Experience with only a simple search-and-answer (RAG) setup is not enough.

- You have measured the quality of an LLM system with evaluation sets or observability, and can give a concrete example. Experience with tools like MLflow and LiteLLM is a plus.

- You have back-end experience, including building REST APIs.

- You have experience in Kubernetes. Experience with Postgres is useful.

- Experience in a legal, tax or other knowledge-intensive domain is a plus.

WHAT YOU'RE SIGNING UP FOR 

On Tuesdays and Thursdays, the team works together at the office. What colleagues value most here: mutual trust, room to experiment, and a team that helps each other out when someone gets stuck.

- A good base salary and a standard working week of 36 hours.

- An end-of-year bonus of 4% of your gross annual salary and variable profit sharing of up to 6% of your gross annual salary.

- 23 holidays and a personal choice budget of 12%, of which 8% is holiday allowance and 4% you can spend freely, for example on extra days off.

- A good pension scheme through PGB, including additional partner insurance.

- A travel allowance of €0.25 per kilometre or a public transport allowance, plus an attractive bike scheme. For employees who live less than 10 km or more than 60 km away, we have a tailored arrangement.

- Hybrid working: two days a week at the office in The Hague, on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

- Room to grow. In your field, in your role, in the organisation.

WANT TO KNOW MORE? 

We'd love to tell you everything about the team and the role. Send us your CV and you'll hear from us within 2 working days. Any questions first? Text or call Nadine at 0628556265.

A reference check and a VOG (certificate of good behaviour) are part of the selection process.

title: Summer Intern 2027
description:
About Lendable

Lendable is on a mission to build the world's best technology to help people get credit and save money. We're building one of the world’s leading fintech companies and are off to a strong start:

- One of the UK’s most exciting unicorns with a team of over 800 people

- Among the fastest-growing tech companies in the UK

- Profitable since 2017 

- Backed by top investors including Balderton Capital and Goldman Sachs 

- Loved by customers with the best reviews in the market (4.9 across 10,000s of reviews on Trustpilot )

So far, we’ve rebuilt the Big Three consumer finance products from scratch: loans, credit cards and car finance . We get money into our customers’ hands in minutes instead of days.

We’re growing fast, and there’s a lot more to do: we’re going after the two biggest Western markets (UK and US) where trillions worth of financial products are held by big banks with dated systems and painful processes. 

Join us if you want to

- Take ownership: you are trusted to make decisions that drive a material impact on the direction and success of Lendable from day 1

- Work in small teams of exceptional people: Lendies are relentlessly resourceful. We challenge the status quo to solve problems and find smarter solutions

- Build the best technology in-house : we use new data sources, machine learning and AI to make machines do the heavy lifting

About the role 

This is a 10 week internship program starting from 29th June 2027 

Salary - £50,000 (per annum) 

We’re looking for a super smart student who is great with numbers and loves problem solving to come and apply your skills in a start up environment a nd have a big impact on our business and how we do things.

What you'll be doing 

- Use your analytical and problem-solving skills to generate key insights from data, and use that insight to drive meaningful change in our strategy

- Using data and modelling to ground assumptions for our NPV model, such as predicting what default rates will be in the future, and using that to inform our lending deicsions

- Using data and analytics to drive decisions about who we should lend to, and how much we should lend to them, and how that changes with the economy and competition changes

- Conducting hypothesis testing, and using your findings to change how we do things in areas such as lending strategy, pricing, and fraud detection

- Presenting your findings to senior leaders in the company, then work with the product/tech team to get them implemented

What we're looking for 

- A university student in their penultimate year (can be undergraduates, masters or PhD students)

- Must have coding skills in Python or SQL 

- Someone that loves numbers ! You’ll be working with numbers every single day in this role so you’ll be able to demonstrate your ability to work with complex data sets, analyse them and draw insights

- You’ll have a natural curiosity and love to dig into things to understand how they work 

- Startup mindset . We’re a fast-growth tech startup so you’ll be super excited to work in an entrepreneurial environment and have a real impact on the business

Interview Process 

- 15-minute online test

- Coding Take Home Task

- Remote (video call) Task Debrief (60 mins)

- Remote (video call) case study (60 mins)

- In-person case study (60 min) + Culture Add Conversation (15 minutes) + a chance to meet other recent grads over lunch (30-45 minutes)

Life at Lendable

- Winning team: the opportunity to scale up one of the world’s most successful fintech companies

- Flexible working: flexible approach tailored to each role. Hybrid roles require three days in-office weekly; fully remote roles include regular opportunities for in-person connection through socials and off-sites

- Socials & connection: opportunities and events to come together, socialise, and get to know each other beyond the office walls

- Health coverage: support for your physical and mental wellbeing, including private health cover

- Retirement & savings: long-term financial wellbeing through retirement savings plans

- Employee referral programme: earn a competitive bonus when you refer successful new team members

- Office meals & snacks: enjoy a fully stocked kitchen, plus complimentary lunches prepared by in-house chefs on in-office days at select locations

- Sustainable commuting: cycle-to-work and electric vehicle salary sacrifice schemes available in select locations

Please note: The availability and details of specific benefits vary by location and role. For more information, please speak to your Talent Partner. 

Check out our blog !

title: Founders Associate (IT & Automation)
description:
Your Role at Lio

At Lio, we’re building a fast-growing AI company and we want our internal operations to reflect the technology we build.

As a Founder’s Associate Intern/ Working Student focused on IT & Automation, you’ll own our day-to-day IT operations and build the systems that help us scale. You’ll make sure people have the tools, access, and support they need, then look for ways to make those processes simpler, more reliable and increasingly automated.

One day, you might be setting up laptops, onboarding a new colleague, or troubleshooting our office network. The next, you could be connecting systems through APIs, building an internal tool or creating an AI agent that saves the team hours of manual work.

Make it work. Make it better. Then automate it. 

You’ll work closely with our CTO, own projects from problem to implementation and see the impact of your work across the company.

What You’ll Do 

- Everyday IT operations. Manage onboarding and offboarding, configure devices and accounts, resolve day-to-day IT issues, and keep our office network running reliably.

- Build IT that scales. Improve how we manage SaaS tools, access permissions, and device security, creating clear processes that grow with the team.

- Turn repetitive work into automated workflows. Find manual tasks across IT and business operations, identify where automation adds value, and build solutions that save time and reduce errors.

- Build practical internal tools. Use AI-assisted coding, Python, APIs, and low-code platforms to solve real operational problems.

- Connect our systems. Integrate Microsoft 365, Slack, and other SaaS platforms so information flows smoothly and teams spend less time switching between tools.

- Put AI to work. Test AI agents and emerging automation tools, turning useful experiments into reliable solutions the team can use.

- Drive improvements with the founders. Identify bottlenecks, propose a better approach, and take ownership of delivering it from the first idea through rollout and ongoing improvement.

Why Join Lio? 

Lio is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and built at Y Combinator . We're bringing Silicon Valley ambition and engineering culture to Munich.

From day one, you'll work with Fortune 500 companies across Europe and the US, solving real-world technical challenges at the intersection of AI and enterprise software.

We move fast, care deeply about execution, and give engineers ownership from day one. The solutions you build won't stay customer-specific and they'll shape the future of our platform.

If you're excited about building with us, we'd love to hear from you.

Any questions about the role? Feel free to reach out to Anika.

title: Android Engineer
description:
About Motorway 

Motorway is the UK's largest online car-selling platform. We connect private sellers directly with over 8,000 dealers nationwide. Our online platform helps sellers achieve great prices for their cars while giving dealers fast, reliable access to the stock they want for their dealerships. Founded in 2017, our award-winning, technology-led approach has redefined the experience of selling a car. Motorway is backed by some of the world’s leading technology investors, having raised £143 million in Series C funding.

This is a unique opportunity to join a fast-growing scale-up at a crucial phase of growth and help change an industry for the better.

👋 Hi, I’m Manuele Maggi, Engineering Manager at Motorway. I’m looking for an Android

Engineer to join our Mobile Engineering group and help us build a best-in-class experience

for our Sellers.

This is a great opportunity to join a talented and supportive team, working alongside

engineers, product managers and designers to fundamentally change the way people sell

their car. You’ll contribute to meaningful features used by customers across the UK, develop

your technical skills and explore the latest tools and technologies—with AI increasingly

embedded in how we build and work.

About the role 

As an Android Engineer, you’ll take ownership of well-defined features and contribute

throughout the development lifecycle, from early ideas through to release and iteration.

Day-to-day, you’ll be:

- Collaborating with designers, product managers and other engineers to build high-quality customer experiences.

- Designing, building and shipping Android features using Kotlin and Jetpack Compose.

- Contributing to the development of our in-house Server-Driven UI framework, helping us deliver features and dynamic experiences more quickly.

- Supporting and improving our mobile infrastructure, including CI/CD pipelines with

- GitHub Actions, Google Play deployment workflows and automated UI testing.

- Writing clean, maintainable and well-tested code.

- Participating in code reviews and technical discussions, learning from others while sharing your own ideas.

- Paying close attention to UI detail, accessibility and the overall app experience.

- Building an understanding of the backend systems and APIs that power our app.

- Monitoring released features and helping to resolve issues when they arise.

- Contributing to the engineering standards and practices used across the Mobile Engineering group.

About you 

- We’re looking for someone with:

- Commercial experience building Android applications.

- Good knowledge of Kotlin and modern Android development.

- Experience with Jetpack Compose, or an interest in developing your skills with it.

- An understanding of common mobile development principles, patterns and testing practices.

- Experience building and releasing features as part of a collaborative product team.

- The ability to write clear, maintainable and well-tested code.

- Good collaboration and communication skills.

- A proactive approach and willingness to take ownership of your work.

- Curiosity and a genuine desire to continue learning and developing as an engineer.

You could be a great fit if 

- You’ve contributed to reusable components or modules.

- You enjoy working closely with product and design to solve customer problems.

- You’re comfortable owning features while asking for support when needed.

- You care about building polished, reliable and accessible mobile experiences.

- You’re interested in using modern technologies, including AI, to improve products and engineering workflows.

- You enjoy sharing ideas, receiving feedback and learning from experienced engineers.

Bonus 

- You don’t need to tick every box, but it would be helpful if:

- You have experience with Server-Driven UI.

- You have worked with A/B testing or experimentation.

- You have some exposure to CI/CD and automated mobile testing.

- You have integrated ML or AI-powered functionality into an app.

- You have experience or an interest in backend or full-stack development.

- Collaborate effectively across engineering, ML, and product teams, communicating clearly in cross-functional settings

Strong candidates may also have experience with:

title: Senior C++/iOS Engineer - User Platform
description:
We’re looking for a Senior C++/iOS Engineer to join the Baldur squad within User Platform (UP). Baldur owns Spotify ’s Session Management and Delegated Authorization domains—the systems that enable applications to securely obtain, use, and manage access tokens for hundreds of millions of users. In this role, you’ll help shape the technology that powers secure access across every Spotify client and third-party integration. 

Your work will support engineers across Spotify building mobile and desktop experiences, platform teams, and third-party developers integrating with Spotify’s authorization platform. You’ll collaborate across disciplines to build secure, reliable, and scalable authentication experiences that have a direct impact on millions of people every day.

What You'll Do

- Collaborate with a highly autonomous and supportive engineering squad responsible for Spotify’s delegated authorization and session management platforms.

- Design, build, and evolve critical infrastructure powering Spotify applications and partner integrations using shared C++ libraries and native Swift on iOS.

- Develop secure, reliable, and performant delegated authorization flows, including token issuance, refresh, revocation, and session lifecycle management across multiple platforms.

- Partner with client and backend engineers to integrate with core authorization services, token issuance, client registration, and token revocation.

- Improve how credentials and access tokens are securely stored and managed on-device while balancing security, reliability, and application performance.

- Contribute to the evolution of Spotify’s authorization frameworks, Spotify-specific implementations, enabling new platforms and product experiences.

- Drive technical improvements, share knowledge with teammates, and help shape the long-term technical direction of delegated authorization and session management.

Who You Are

- You have strong proficiency in C++, along with experience building native iOS applications in Swift, or you're excited to develop your expertise in Swift while applying your C++ skills.

- You have experience designing, building, or maintaining security-sensitive systems such as authorization, authentication, token management, credential storage, or related platforms.

- You bring a systems-thinking mindset and enjoy solving complex engineering challenges that span client and backend technologies.

- You have a solid understanding of software architecture, secure system design, and modern authorization protocols such as OAuth 2.0.

- You approach problems thoughtfully, with strong attention to detail and a focus on building secure, reliable, and maintainable solutions.

- You communicate clearly and enjoy collaborating with engineers across multiple teams and technical disciplines.

- You have experience working with shared cross-platform codebases and understand how native platform layers interact with common C++ libraries.

- You enjoy working on large-scale distributed systems where your contributions improve experiences for hundreds of millions of Spotify users.

Where You'll Be

- This role is based in London or Stockholm. 

- We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Compensation

Additional Information

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.

At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

title: Ubuntu Linux Kernel Test Engineer
description:
Ubuntu is the most widely used Linux distribution in the world, delivering kernels across a vast matrix of versions, architectures, and configurations – with up to 15 years of security and maintenance commitments for Long Term Support (LTS) releases. Ensuring the quality and reliability of these kernels demands a dedicated, systematic approach to testing at scale.

The Canonical Kernel Team is looking for a Test Engineer to take ownership of our kernel testing strategy and infrastructure. You will design and maintain test plans covering functional correctness, stability, performance, and security. You will build and evolve automated test frameworks – including stress testing, fuzzing, code coverage analysis, and regression detection – that not only must remain effective across many concurrently supported kernel versions spanning years of maintenance, but must be able to scale with the high demand for Ubuntu kernels (currently more than 160 under active support).

The successful candidate will bring strong Python skills, familiarity with Linux kernel internals, and experience building test infrastructure that scales. You will work closely with kernel engineers to catch regressions early, validate fixes, and ensure every kernel we ship meets the highest standards of reliability.

Location: This role will be based remotely in the APAC region, except for Taipei, Taiwan, and Beijing, China, which are office-based locations.

What your day will look like

- Design, develop, and maintain comprehensive test plans covering functional correctness, stability, performance, and security for Ubuntu Linux kernels

- Build and improve automated test infrastructure for continuous kernel quality validation across multiple kernel versions and architectures

- Maintain long-lived test suites that evolve alongside Ubuntu’s many concurrently supported kernel versions spanning years of maintenance

- Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines for continuous kernel quality validation

- Conduct performance benchmarking and regression detection across kernel releases

- Measure and improve kernel code coverage, identifying gaps in test coverage and creating tests to address them

- Execute and analyze stress tests covering CPU scheduling, memory management, I/O subsystems, networking, and filesystem workloads

- Develop and maintain fuzzing harnesses to discover kernel vulnerabilities and reliability issues using tools such as syzkaller, Trinity, or custom fuzzers

- Collaborate regularly and proactively with a globally distributed team

- Contribute to upstream test suites and testing frameworks

- Document test methodologies, results, and coverage gaps

What we are looking for in you

- Significant programming experience in Python

- Experience with test frameworks such as LTP, kselftest, xfstests, stress-ng, fio, or similar

- Experience designing and executing system-level tests: functional, stress, performance, or regression testing

- Familiarity with CI/CD systems (Jenkins, GitHub CI, or similar)

- Experience maintaining test suites over long periods, adapting to evolving software across multiple supported versions

- Familiarity with Linux (Ubuntu or Debian preferred but not required), Linux kernel internals and subsystems

- Experience with Linux systems administration and automation

- Solid background with git

- Well-organized, self-starting and able to deliver to fixed schedules

- Professional written and spoken English with excellent communication skills

- Ability to travel twice a year, for company events up to two weeks each

Additional skills that you might also bring

- Familiarity with kernel fuzzing tools and techniques (e.g. syzkaller, Trinity, AFL, or custom harnesses)

- Experience with code coverage instrumentation (e.g. gcov, kcov, LLVM source-based coverage)

- Knowledge of kernel tracing and observability tools (e.g. ftrace, perf, bpftrace, eBPF)

- Familiarity with static analysis tools (e.g. sparse, smatch, Coccinelle) as part of a testing workflow

- Experience with fault injection frameworks (e.g. failslab, fail_make_request) for reliability testing

- Prior experience with test infrastructure at scale (provisioning, orchestration, result aggregation)

- Experience with Ubuntu/Debian packaging or Snap

- Knowledge of virtualization technologies (KVM, QEMU) and container runtimes

- Cloud infrastructure experience (AWS, GCP, Azure, or OpenStack)

- Prior involvement with open source testing communities or projects

What we offer you

Your base pay will depend on various factors including your geographical location, level of experience, knowledge and skills. In addition to the benefits above, certain roles are also eligible for additional benefits and rewards including annual bonuses and sales incentives based on revenue or utilisation. Our compensation philosophy is to ensure equity right across our global workforce. 

In addition to a competitive base pay, we provide all team members with additional benefits, which reflect our values and ideals. Please note that additional benefits may apply depending on the work location and, for more information on these, you can ask in the later stages of the recruitment process.

- Fully remote working environment - we’ve been working remotely since 2004!

- Personal learning and development budget of 2,000USD per annum

- Annual compensation review

- Recognition rewards

- Annual holiday leave

- Parental Leave

- Employee Assistance Programme

- Opportunity to travel to new locations to meet colleagues at ‘sprints’

- Priority Pass for travel and travel upgrades for long haul company events

Canonical is a pioneering tech firm that is at the forefront of the global move to open source. As the company that publishes Ubuntu, one of the most important open source projects and the platform for AI, IoT and the cloud, we are changing the world on a daily basis. We recruit on a global basis and set a very high standard for people joining the company. We expect excellence - in order to succeed, we need to be the best at what we do.

Canonical has been a remote-first company since its inception in 2004.​ Work at Canonical is a step into the future, and will challenge you to think differently, work smarter, learn new skills, and raise your game. Canonical provides a unique window into the world of 21st-century digital business.

title: Senior ML Engineer | Kimchi (Inference Stack Optimization)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and we run the models underneath it ourselves.

Kimchi Inference 

One API line and a customer's existing client just works: DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, MiniMax, Nemotron served serverless from our own GPU fleet (OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible, pay per token, spend visible per user, team, and key). When control matters, the same models run on the customer's own cluster instead. Behind that one line sits the machinery you'll own: SGLang and vLLM engines, B300 nodes, a shared cluster filesystem that holds every checkpoint exactly once, KV caches riding coding traffic with heavy prefix reuse, and the benchmark harness that gates every change we ship.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Throughput. Latency. Cold starts. Cost per token.

Move those four numbers in the right direction and two things happen: customers get faster, cheaper inference, and our margins improve. That's the entire thesis of this role. Every loader you tune, every scheduler decision you land, every kernel you stare at shows up in a customer's p99 and on our P&L. Your mandate is the inference stack's optimization, whatever it takes, and the technical direction of how we optimize it is yours to argue with data.

The problem: the checkpoints run 0.3-1.5 TB, and the "right" serving configuration depends on traffic shape, sequence-length distribution, batch dynamics, GPU SKU, memory bandwidth, and quantization tolerance, all variables that shift week to week. Most teams pick a configuration once, over-provision GPUs, and absorb the cost. We don't: we took Kimi-K3 (1.5 TB) from over an hour cold-to-serving to under twelve minutes with a shared filesystem, O_DIRECT weight loaders, and node-local JIT caches, and we're nowhere near done. Prefill/decode disaggregation and tiered KV caches are next.

Stack: Python; SGLang; vLLM; TensorRT-LLM; PyTorch; fastsafetensors; CUDA-adjacent tooling; Kubernetes; virtiofs shared filesystems; ClickHouse; OpenTelemetry; Prometheus; Grafana; GitLab CI.

Requirements

- You've built real ML systems for 5+ years, and your portfolio shows depth in inference or training infrastructure, not just model training notebooks.

- Your Python is production-grade: services, not scripts.

- You've run vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM for real, and you have a working mental model of why an engine performs the way it does on a given GPU.

- You've measured quantization regressions, not just compression ratios.

- Multi-GPU and multi-node setups hold no fear: tensor and expert parallelism, collective communication, and their practical failure modes.

- You know where the bytes live (page caches, O_DIRECT, network filesystems under terabyte-scale reads) and how fast they move.

- You instrument before you optimize, and you can tell a real win from a benchmark artifact.

- A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

- You've worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.

- Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.

- You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

Responsibilities

- Push throughput. Continuous batching, chunked prefill, speculative decoding with draft models, CUDA-graph capture, and scheduler tuning across the engine
fleet. Find the ceiling on each GPU SKU, then raise it.

- Cut latency. Attack TTFT and inter-token latency separately; profile to find the actual bottleneck (compute, memory bandwidth, scheduling, storage, or
network) and fix it, not the one you assumed.

- Get more out of the KV cache. Hierarchical and paged attention, prefix caching on heavy-reuse coding traffic, eviction policies, quantized KV. A lot of the
unrealized throughput lives here, and you'll own it.

- Kill cold starts. Weight loaders (O_DIRECT, fastsafetensors-class), JIT and compile caches, shared-filesystem read paths. A 1.5 TB checkpoint has no business
taking an hour to reach serving.

- Quantize without regressing quality. INT8/INT4, FP8/FP4 across weights, activations, and KV, measured on real workloads, not just perplexity benchmarks.

- Scale across nodes. Distributed inference topologies, network-aware placement, prefill/decode disaggregation, checkpointing strategies that don't bottleneck
on storage or interconnect.

- Set the technical direction. Decide what we benchmark, what we adopt, and what we build ourselves. Bring the team along with strong writeups and reproducible
experiments.

What’s in it for you?

- Competitive salary (depending on the level of experience).

- Enjoy a flexible, remote-first global environment.

- Collaborate with a global team of cloud experts and innovators, passionate about pushing the boundaries of Kubernetes technology

- Equity options.

- Get quick feedback with a fast-paced workflow. Most feature projects are completed in 1 to 4 weeks.

- Team-building budget and company events to connect with your colleagues.

- Equipment budget to ensure you have everything you need.

title: Senior Applied ML Engineer | Kimchi (Model Router)
description:
Why Kimchi?

Great models are raw ingredients. Kimchi is what happens when you ferment them with good engineering. We started inside CAST AI helping companies run LLMs on their own Kubernetes clusters; today we run our own coding harness on any model you pick, and the router deciding which model answers each request is ours too.

The Auto Router 

Our promise is one enforcement layer for your AI: budgets, spend attribution, and model routing, applied before a request ever hits a model. The Auto Router makes the call: for every request, which model serves it. Eight open-source models whose input prices span more than 20×, cached input up to 50× cheaper than fresh, frontier providers on customers' own keys, and a coding agent that fires hundreds of requests before its task is done. Frontier-level task success at a fraction of the token cost: that sentence is the product, and it stays true only if the model inside the router keeps getting better. That model is yours.

Made by Cast AI — a Miami-headquartered, globally distributed team across 34 countries that hit unicorn status in January 2026 with a $50B+ backed investment pushing its valuation past $1 billion. 

About the role

Every request gets a decision: which model serves it.

This is an applied-ML seat, not an infrastructure one. Platform engineers own the proxy, the streaming path, and the fleet. You own the model inside them: the training data, the objective, the evaluation, and the iteration loop that ships a better router every cycle.

The problem: routing is a prediction problem wearing a product's clothes. For every request you predict the quality each candidate model would deliver, what it would cost, and how fast it would decode, and you have to be right enough, in aggregate, that the savings are real and the quality never dips below frontier. The data is messy: rollout outcomes from benchmark harnesses, per-request records from the live fleet, override signals, and token streams whose speed depends on the serving concurrency at the moment. Speed itself is a correctness variable: on deadline-bound agentic work, a model that decodes three times slower doesn't do the same work slower, it does less work. That's why naive cost-per-token objectives quietly optimize for the wrong thing. And the bar for evidence is high: a router change ships only after production-parity evaluation with error bars, then gets held to its numbers in live traffic.

Stack: Python; PyTorch; SQL at scale (ClickHouse); OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible LLM APIs; benchmark and rollout harnesses (RouterBench-class); GitLab CI.

Requirements

- You've spent 5+ years in applied ML or ML research, and you've trained, evaluated, and shipped models that make real-time decisions (ranking, recommendation, bandits, pricing, or LLM routing) and you can tell that story with receipts.

- Strong Python and SQL at scale: you can pull, clean, and interrogate millions of request-level records without waiting on anyone.

- You know the difference between a model that got better and an eval that got easier.

- You have real opinions about what LLM benchmarks measure, agentic harnesses included.

- You know enough serving reality (TTFT, decode speed, batching, prefix caching, concurrency) to model the objective honestly.

- You instrument before you optimize, error bars and all.

- A wide mandate excites you more than it unsettles you.

Nice to haves

- You've worked on LLM routing specifically: RouterBench-class evals, cost/quality/latency Pareto fronts.

- Calibration, abstention, or conformal methods in production decision systems.

- You've run online A/B loops with drift monitoring on a model that touches real money.

Responsibilities

- Own the routing model end to end: features, objective, training, calibration, and release cadence. Iterate it like a product, not a research artifact.

- Build the evaluation that gates every change: production-parity benchmarks, router-vs-router comparisons, holdouts by task family, error bars on pass rates.
Nothing ships on vibes.

- Turn fleet data into training signal: per-request outcomes from production, benchmark rollouts, and override feedback, with failure categorization (infra vs
task) so poisoned labels never reach the policy.

- Model the objective the user actually experiences: task success × token cost × wall-clock speed under the real concurrency regime, with cached-input
economics in the picture.

- Run the online loop: shadow, A/B, full rollout, drift monitoring, retrain. When production disagrees with your offline eval, you find out why before the next
ship.

- Push the frontier where it pays: calibrated decisions, abstention under uncertainty, speed-aware routing. We experiment on what a router should be, not just
which model it picks today.

- Partner with platform engineers on instrumentation: the features and labels recorded per request (decode speed first-class among them) and the experiments
the data path must support.

What’s in it for you?

title: Director of Quality
description:
About LILT 

AI is changing how the world communicates — and LILT is leading that transformation. 

We're on a mission to make the world's information accessible to everyone , regardless of the language they speak. We use cutting-edge AI, machine translation, and human-in-the-loop expertise to translate content faster, more accurately, and more cost-effectively without compromising on brand, voice, or quality.

At LILT, we empower our teammates with leading tools, global collaboration, and growth opportunities to do their best work. Our company virtues— Work together, win together; Find a way or make one; Dance in the customer's shoes; Quicker than they expect; Quality is Job 1 —guide everything we do. We are trusted by Intel Corporation , Canva , the United States Department of Defense , the United States Air Force , ASICS , and hundreds of global Enterprises. Backed by Sequoia, Intel Capital, and Redpoint, we’re building a category-defining company in a $50B+ global translation market being redefined by AI.

Location: Remote or hybrid, EMEA or US Eastern time zone

Team: Production, Quality

Reports to: VP Production

Direct reports: Quality Manager (AMER, customer staffing) and 2 Quality Coordinators

About the role

As Director of Quality, you will own LILT's quality system end to end: standards, audit, compliance, procedures, continuous improvement, and the roadmap and operation of our Quality Agents . You'll help move Quality from a primarily reactive, execution-led function to a proactive, data-driven partner for customers and internal teams, with quality designed into our AI-native workflows.

You'll be the person who can run a customer audit while simultaneously shipping an improved agent evaluation. As the single Quality partner for Customer Success, Production, Research and Product, you'll turn customer requirements into measurable acceptance criteria, effective controls and better models and workflows. You'll advise customers on the right quality, cost and speed mix, including where automated, agent-verified and human-verified workflows are appropriate, with stronger assurance for high-risk and regulated content.

We're looking for a hands-on Quality SME and operator with real depth in both worlds: experience designing and building AI agents and improving LLM output, and a solid grounding in traditional quality management. You'll bring senior expertise in data, AI, customer advisory and process, and make sure quality work prevents recurrence rather than stopping at rework or ticket closure.

What you'll do

Quality Agent leadership 

- Evaluate, design and build reliable Quality Agents with well-defined tools and clear, structured instructions.

- Use orchestration patterns to evolve from a single agent to multi-agent systems.

- Define evaluation criteria, test sets and success metrics for agent performance, and run agents in production with clear monitoring and escalation paths.

- Drive adoption across teams and show measurable reductions in manual quality effort.

Research and Product partnership 

- Work closely with Research and Product on ADQ, LLM model improvements, AI Review, AI QA, and new and emerging AI workflows.

- Turn quality findings into product requirements, evaluation criteria and continuous feedback loops that improve model and workflow output.

- Act as the voice of quality in roadmap discussions, and help decide where human review, AI review or both are needed.

Audit, compliance and procedure 

- Own LILT's approach to internal and external audits, including ISO certification (e.g. ISO 17100, ISO 18587, ISO 9001) and customer audits.

- Plan and run periodic internal audits, manage evidence collection, and track corrective and preventive actions to closure.

- Standardise and maintain SOPs, workflows and quality documentation, and keep them current as AI workflows change how we work.

- Make sure quality processes meet customer, contractual and regulatory requirements.

Customer advisory 

- Partner with Customer Success and Delivery to define proactive quality programmes, success metrics and governance for strategic accounts, including AI-forward enterprise and life science / regulatory programmes.

- Translate customer quality requirements into clear pre-delivery acceptance criteria, validation methods and risk-appropriate controls.

- Advise customers on the right quality, cost and speed mix and where automated, agent-verified, human-verified or combined workflows are appropriate.

- Represent LILT's quality function as a credible subject-matter authority in customer business reviews, audits and escalations, using quality data and metrics to demonstrate fitness for purpose.

Continuous improvement 

- Lead structured CI across the Commercial business: root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, KPI reviews and retrospectives.

title: Staff Applied AI Researcher (Agentic Search)

About Nebius: 

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

We are seeking a Staff Applied AI Researcher to join a fast growing team building an agent native search platform - the web access layer for AI systems.

You can think of this as Google for AI agents: a system designed for machines, not humans. We are building agentic search, where AI systems actively plan, retrieve, evaluate, and refine information rather than simply returning results. As AI becomes the primary interface to the web, this layer will replace the role of traditional search engines.

We are designing how AI agents - not humans - retrieve, evaluate, and reason over web data in real time, under strict latency and reliability constraints. This means solving retrieval and ranking under entirely new access patterns and at significant scale, with systems operating over constantly changing, unstructured data and serving tens of thousands of production workloads 24 by 7.

This role comes with ownership over key parts of our applied AI research direction and system design, with a strong expectation of defining new approaches and shipping measurable impact in production.

What you'll work on: 

- Designing agent native retrieval systems optimised for machine consumption rather than human search UX

- Building systems where LLMs iteratively plan, query, refine, and reason over results

- Developing ranking and retrieval approaches for multi step, agent driven workflows under real world constraints

Your responsibilites: 

- Drive applied research and technical direction across retrieval and ranking systems

- Design and evolve multi stage retrieval architectures (query understanding, rewriting, reranking, iterative retrieval)

- Develop methods for grounding LLMs in real time web data at scale

- Define and implement new evaluation paradigms and metrics for agentic systems, where correctness is not reducible to clicks

- Lead experimentation on modern retrieval approaches (embeddings, hybrid search, reranking) and bring them into production

- Analyse trade-offs across relevance, latency, and cost at scale

- Work closely with engineering to deploy systems in high throughput, low latency environments

- Own ambiguous problems end to end and contribute to product and research direction

- Mentor engineers and help raise the technical bar of the team

Must haves: 

- 8+ years of experience in applied AI, ML, or software engineering

- Proven track record of shipping ML or AI systems to production at scale

- Deep experience with search, retrieval, ranking, recommendation systems, or assistants

- Strong understanding of modern deep learning, especially transformers and embeddings

- Experience with LLM integrated or knowledge intensive systems

- Experience designing evaluation frameworks and metrics for ML systems

- Strong programming skills in Python and at least one of Go, C++, or similar

- Ability to operate in a fast moving, product driven environment with high ownership and autonomy

Nice to haves 

- Experience with large scale search or recommendation systems

- Background in agentic AI systems (agents, tool use, autonomous workflows)

- Experience with RAG, multi step retrieval, or tool use

- Publications, open source, or similar signals of technical depth and impact

Benefits & Perks: 

- Competitive compensation

- Career growth and learning opportunities

- Flexibility and ownership

- Collaborative and innovative culture

- Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects

- International environment and talented teams

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

title: Principal MEMS Development Engineer
description:
About SiTime 

SiTime Corporation is the precision timing company. Our semiconductor MEMS programmable solutions offer a rich feature set that enables customers to differentiate their products with higher performance, smaller size, lower power and better reliability. With more than 3 billion devices shipped, SiTime is changing the timing industry. For more information, visit www.sitime.com .

Job Summary 

Join the team that is revolutionizing the timing industry with the best silicon Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS) timing products in the world. As a Principal MEMS Development Engineer, you will use your technical and creative problem-solving skills to push forward MEMS technology and engineer resonators for SiTime’s next-generation timing products. It is not necessary to meet all job requirements to be a qualified candidate for the position.

Responsibilities: 

- Lead definition and execution of challenging technical projects. 

- Advise management of challenges, impact, recommendations.

- Develop new or improved resonators, MEMS technologies and/or products.

- Design MEMS devices and characterize their electrical, mechanical, and thermal performance on wafer level and/or device level. 

- Work with process team to drive continuous improvement in MEMS yields.

- Extend and enhance automated infrastructure for MEMS design, measurements, and data analysis.

- Design and analyze experiments to understand device physics, materials, and fabrication.

- Interface with local and overseas vendors.

- Work in cross-functional teams, including circuits, systems, and packaging.

- Working/supporting other projects as needed.

Qualifications & Requirements: 

- Ph.D. in ME, EE, Physics, or equivalent

- At least 3 years of industry experience.

- Skilled scientist with ability to design, conduct, and analyze experiments.

- Excellent problem identification and problem-solving abilities.

- Excellent knowledge of mechanics, electrodynamics, thermodynamics.

- Knowledge in fundamentals of MEMS devices physics and fabrication.

- Experience with finite element simulation tools (COMSOL, ANSYS) and data processing tools (Matlab, Python).

- Excellent interpersonal, organizational, written and verbal communication skills.

- Passion for delivering exceptional results.

Desired Characteristics & Attributes: 

- 3 -10 years of industry experience.

- Intermediate to advanced knowledge of programing languages, circuits, metrology equipment and methods.

- Experience with Statistical analysis and tools such as R or JMP.

- Knowledge in MEMS microfabrication.

Compensation Range: 

At SiTime, we believe great work deserves great rewards. We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive compensation package designed to attract top talent. 

In addition to base salary, this role is eligible for a quarterly bonus tied to the achievement of innovation goals—reflecting our commitment to recognizing meaningful impact. We also offer equity grants, providing a meaningful opportunity to share in the company’s future growth and success.

SiTime is an Equal Opportunity Employer . We treat each person fairly and we do not tolerate discrimination or harassment against anyone on the basis of any protected characteristics, including race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, pregnancy, political affiliation, protected veteran status, protected genetic information, or marital status or other characteristics protected by law. 

Learn More about SiTime: Review the Get to Know SiTime section of our career page to explore our culture, values, and what makes us unique.

title: Analytics Engineer, Revenue, Purchase & Order
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third. 
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Information about the position 

We are looking for an Analytics Engineer to join our Revenue, Purchase & Order Analytics Engineering team.

The area sits at the heart of some of the most critical customer journeys and commercial systems across Vinted’s Marketplace Business Unit, spanning Revenue (pricing and advertising), Purchase (inquiries and checkout), and Orders (transactions and fulfilment). Together, these domains create a rich, high-volume, and deeply interconnected data ecosystem.

As an Analytics Engineer, you’ll work at the intersection of data, engineering, and product, building trusted data products that power business and product decision-making across these domains.

In this position, you’ll 

- Build scalable data products: Design, develop, and evolve reliable, cost-efficient data products and pipelines that power analytics and machine learning use cases across the domains.

- Build quality in by design: Embed automated testing, validation, and quality controls throughout the data lifecycle to ensure data remains accurate, consistent, and complete.

- Strengthen observability: Improve monitoring and alerting to detect and address issues before they impact downstream consumers.

- Own production reliability: Take end-to-end ownership of production data systems, from investigating incidents and diagnosing root causes to implementing durable fixes that prevent recurrence and improve long-term resilience.

Who you’ll work with:

- Revenue, Purchase & Order Analytics Engineering: Join a talented and driven team of 7+ Analytics Engineers, working across interconnected domains and tackling complex, high-impact data challenges.

- Data & Decision Scientists: Work closely with Data Scientists and Decision Scientists to build trusted data foundations that enable better business and product decisions.

- Engineering, Product & Business: Partner with Backend Engineering, Product, and Business teams to understand their needs, shape technical requirements, and translate them into well-designed, trusted data solutions.

- The Analytics Engineering Guild: Be an active member of Vinted’s 40+ member AE Guild, benefiting from shared tooling, engineering standards, and knowledge across domains. You’ll also have opportunities to contribute to “side quests” that improve engineering practices, tooling, and reusable capabilities.

About you 

- Experience working as an Analytics Engineer, Data Engineer, or in a closely related data role.

- Strong SQL and data warehousing fundamentals, with the ability to build clean, performant, and maintainable data solutions.

- Hands-on experience with dbt or a similar data transformation framework, building well-structured and tested data models.

- Experience working with a cloud data warehouse such as BigQuery, Snowflake, Redshift, or similar.

- A solid understanding of data modelling principles and their application to real-world analytical problems.

- Familiarity with workflow orchestration tools such as Airflow, Dagster, or similar.

- Comfortable working with high-volume, business-critical data, balancing a high bar for quality and reliability with a pragmatic bias for action.

- Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to clearly explain technical concepts and trade-offs to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Work perks 

- The opportunity to benefit from our share options programme

- 25 days of paid annual leave

- Newest MacBook models

- Confidential Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for you and your family

- Frequent team-building events

- Home office support: we provide IT workstation equipment and a personal budget of up to €540 for home workplace furniture

- Lunch benefit per working day

- A personal monthly budget for shopping on Vinted

- Collective Defined Contribution Pension plan

- NS Business Card for your commute to the office by public transport

- Company bike leasing scheme

- Monthly budget for a flexible benefits platform

- Work from Home allowance [[DELETE FOR Breda, Utrecht, Amsterdam Store]] 

- A dog-friendly office

Working at Vinted 

Workation policy 

Better balance holidays with workdays by working remotely! Up to 90 days per year in the EU, of these, 21 days can be spent globally. For non-EU citizens, it's 21 days worldwide. This can be combined with time off for vacation or personal time.

Individual learning budget 

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

Hybrid work 

Our hybrid model, with 2 recommended office days a week, gives you and your team the flexibility to decide if and when you want to work from home, and when to catch up in person.

Equal opportunity 

We welcome applications from everybody, regardless of your background, identity, or life experiences. Job openings come with guides, not checklists. If you’re excited about a role, but don’t identify with every point in the ‘About you’ section, apply anyway – you might still be the perfect match!

The annual gross salary range for this position excluding 8% holiday pay is:

€53.900 — €72.900 EUR

title: Senior Software Engineer, Firefox Security
description:
Why Mozilla? 

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. 

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. 

What you’ll do: 

- Design, build and implement security and hardening features for enterprise users: Design, implement, test, and ship cutting-edge security features that strengthen Firefox’s security posture. 

- Advance Firefox’s security architecture across multiple operating systems: Contribute to and drive cutting-edge improvements to Firefox’s core security posture, by building privilege isolation and moving trust boundaries or Strengthen Firefox’s security architecture: Improve Firefox’s core security mechanisms including cryptographic protocols, WebPKI, and security-sensitive web APIs. 

- Contribute to our security initiatives: Work across teams to investigate security issues, identify root causes, and deliver robust, maintainable fixes. 

- Improve browser reliability and performance: Diagnose and resolve issues affecting stability, correctness, performance, and memory usage in a complex, multithreaded environment. 

What you’ll bring: 

- Systems programming experience and security knowledge: 3+ years of experience in low-level software engineering, strong proficiency in C and/or C++, and a solid understanding of security fundamentals. 

- Debugging and problem-solving skills: Experience diagnosing and resolving issues in multithreaded, cross-platform native applications, including memory and performance challenges. 

- Web platform and modern systems experience: Familiarity with web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) and interest or experience in Rust; ability to work effectively within large, complex, multi-language codebases. 

- Effective collaboration and communication: Experience working with distributed teams and communicating technical ideas clearly in writing and conversation. 

What you’ll get: 

- Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team 

- Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute) 

- Quarterly all-company wellness days where everyone takes a pause together 

- Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday 

- One-time home office stipend 

- Annual professional development budget 

- Quarterly well-being stipend 

- Considerable paid parental leave 

- Employee referral bonus program 

- Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country) 

About Mozilla 

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online.

Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging 

Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission. We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, persons of all sexual orientation s, gender identities, and expressions.

We will ensure that qualified individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, as appropriate. description:
Ditto | Engineering & Product | Remote (US: Atlanta, Austin, SF, Seattle) + APAC | Full-time
https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/ditto https://docs.ditto.live/home/about-ditto I've been obsessed with CRDTs since I first saw them at Strange Loop years ago, and I still can't quite believe I now get to work on them for a living — in some of the most challenging environments there are: disconnected, degraded, contested, out where the cloud isn't. If that's your kind of problem, come build with us. Ditto is the edge-native data platform that keeps distributed systems in sync when the network doesn't cooperate — an offline-first, CRDT-based layer syncing any device (phone, vehicle, sensor, server) over Bluetooth LE, P2P Wi-Fi, LAN, and tactical radio, with or without connectivity. Same core, commercial to defense; operationally deployed and network-agnostic. The problems are the fun kind: conflict-free replication with no server and no synchronized clock, multi-transport routing that never drops the connection, moving a coherent picture over links as thin as an HF radio shot, and human-in-the-loop robotics/autonomy where a detection may have to be physically carried by a moving node. Concept to field in days, not months. Most roles are open to anyone authorized to work in the U.S.; Public Sector and forward-deployed roles require U.S. person status. Airtm is a financial-infrastructure company building the future of the online-work economy. We are on a mission to empower the world's growing number of Digital Entrepreneurs in the Global South, giving them the financial freedom to thrive.

The problem is clear: in emerging markets, accessing the dollar economy is difficult. Cross-border payments are slow, expensive, and often lose value to inflation. This limits the potential of millions of talented individuals.

Airtm’s solution is a swift and comprehensive financial platform that facilitates low-value cross-border payments and local cash-outs. As pioneers in stablecoin-payment infrastructure, Airtm has built the most advanced cross-border payment system available on the market.

As a company married to the world of online work, Airtm will go beyond payments to build the necessary infrastructure the online-work economy needs to thrive. We are fostering an entirely new economy, giving individuals, communities, and countries the tools to take control of their financial destinies.

About the Role: 

The Senior QA Engineer is responsible for ensuring the quality and reliability of the company's software products. This role involves close collaboration with product and engineering teams to define clear acceptance criteria, develop and execute comprehensive test strategies, and build robust automated testing frameworks for a modern web application and its backend services. The engineer plays a critical role in maintaining high standards for product releases and improving the overall quality assurance process, while actively pioneering the integration of AI and LLM tools into the testing lifecycle.

What you’ll be responsible for, the QA engineer: 

- 

- 
Analyzes product specifications to derive comprehensive and testable acceptance criteria.

- 
Collaborates with product managers and developers to clarify requirements and identify potential edge cases.

- 
Designs, implements, and maintains a robust suite of automated tests, including end-to-end, integration, and regression tests.

- 
Performs manual testing for complex or new features prior to the establishment of full automation coverage.

- 
Monitors, analyzes, and improves test coverage, reliability, and performance over time.

- 
Contributes to the continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) process by integrating automated tests into the deployment pipeline.

- 
Enhances overall product quality by creating detailed bug reports, providing constructive feedback, and maintaining clear testing documentation.

- 
Designs and deploys AI-assisted testing workflows to automate recurring tasks such as test case generation, test data synthesis, and log analysis.

- 
Evaluates and integrates LLM-based testing and coding tools into the QA team's workflow, assessing their reliability, accuracy, and fitness for automated testing and edge-case discovery use cases.

Experience and skills required: 

- 

- 
Proven experience as a Senior QA Engineer (5+ Years of experience) or similar role, specifically testing modern web applications and backend services.

- 
Strong proficiency with test automation frameworks such as Cypress, Playwright, or similar tools.

- 
Deep understanding of backend services, APIs (REST and GraphQL), and their common failure scenarios.

- 
Ability to read and comprehend frontend and backend code to assist in debugging and test creation.

- 
Familiarity with version control systems (Git) and CI/CD tools and processes.

- 
Hands-on experience with AI agent frameworks (e.g., LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, or similar) and demonstrated ability to build, deploy, or thoroughly validate agent-assisted testing systems in a near-production context.

- 
Proactive and highly detail-oriented mindset.

- 
Advanced proficiency in the English language.

Applicants must be based in South, North or Central America 

(applications from other locations will not be considered).

This is a fully remote role , reporting to our Tech Lead.

Compensation

title: Software Engineer - Applied AI
description:
About DevRev 

At DevRev, we're building the future of work with Computer – your AI teammate. Unlike traditional tools, Computer unifies all your data sources, tools, and workflows into a single AI-ready platform, giving employees real-time insights, proactive suggestions, and powerful agentic actions. It extends your existing software with AI-native apps and agents that work alongside your teams and customers – updating workflows, coordinating across teams, and eliminating repetitive work. We call this Team Intelligence: human-AI collaboration that breaks down silos, brings people back together, and frees you to solve bigger problems. Backed by Khosla Ventures and Mayfield with $150M+ raised, DevRev is trusted by global companies across industries.

About the Role: 

As a Forward Deployed Engineer at DevRev, you will work closely with our pre- and post-sales Customer Experience team by developing solutions over the core platform via applications written in TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, etc. One of the key functions of this role is, building the Knowledge Graph that includes integration of DevRev with other SaaS and non-SaaS systems through webhooks and APIs and/ or real-time communication architectures. You will be expected to employ your creativity and expertise to ideate and shape how AI, analytics and workflows are used in customers' processes.

What You'll Do: 

- Customer-facing: 30% working directly with customers.

- Coding & Integration: 70-80% hands-on technical implementation 

- Build & Deploy Solutions: Design, develop, and launch AI agents, integrations, and automations that connect DevRev with customers' existing tech stacks and workflows.

- Integrate Systems: Connect DevRev with SaaS and non-SaaS platforms through APIs, webhooks, and real-time communication architectures for seamless data flow.

- Optimize AI Performance: Apply prompt engineering, fine-tune semantic search engines, and leverage generative AI techniques to enhance agent accuracy and user experience.

- Own Data Insights: Write SQL queries, perform data analysis, and build dashboards to surface insights that drive customer decision-making.

- Prototype & Iterate: Develop rapid proofs-of-concept, conduct live technical demos, and refine solutions based on customer and stakeholder feedback.

- Lead Cross-functional Collaboration: Maintain constant communication loops with customers, engineering, product, customer success, support, and revenue teams to ensure alignment.

- Guide Technical Adoption: Learn and master new tools, then guide customers through critical workflows like code repository integrations and advanced configurations.

- Travel Ready: Willingness to travel up to 30% for on-site implementations, technical workshops, and customer engagements.

What You Bring: 

- Experience: 3+ years in software development, systems integration, or platform engineering. Customer-facing experience is a plus.

- Background: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.

- Coding Skills: Strong proficiency in TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, data structures and algorithms. (Nice to have: Go)

- Applied AI Knowledge: Familiarity with large language models (LLMs), prompt engineering, frameworks like RAG and function calling, and building evals to validate agentic AI solutions.

- Integration Expertise: Deep experience with large-scale data synchronization (one-way and two-way), API integration patterns (REST, GraphQL, webhooks), and event-driven/pub/sub architectures.

- Cloud & Deployment: Hands-on experience deploying on serverless and edge platforms (AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions) with modern DevOps practices (CI/CD, containers, observability).

- Data Transformation: Skilled in data mapping, schema alignment, and working with heterogeneous systems. Understanding of data modeling and graph data structures.

- Observability: Experience implementing clear logging, actionable error surfacing, and telemetry to support faster debugging and issue resolution.

- Context-Aware Systems: Familiarity with Model Context Programming (MCP) for building adaptive, context-aware integrations.

- Problem-Solving: Strong track record triaging and unblocking both technical and non-technical blockers to keep projects moving forward.

- Documentation: Experience writing concise, well-structured documentation that supports long-term team understanding and seamless onboarding.

- Communication: Strong written and verbal skills to articulate technical concepts to engineers, product teams, and business stakeholders.
As part of our hiring process, shortlisted candidates will undergo a Background Verification (BGV). By applying, you consent to sharing personal information required for this process. Any offer made will be subject to successful completion of the BGV.

How do we work? 
Whatever your role, our values describe what we ask of each other.

Be a bridger 
Look beyond your own role. Ask questions, share context and help others get unstuck. That may mean bringing the right people together or picking up a problem that doesn’t necessarily fit neatly into your job description.

Care loudly 
We want your perspective, not just your agreement. Speak up when something isn’t working or someone needs support. Give honest feedback with respect for the person receiving it. Don’t let an uncomfortable conversation become an unspoken problem.

Own the outcome 
Take responsibility for the result, not just your part in the process. Use AI to move the work forward, not to outsource your judgment. Make the call, check whether it worked and change course when it didn’t. If something goes wrong, own it and help fix it.

That’s DevRev!

title: Senior Software Engineer, Agents (m/f/x)
description:
About this role 

We are looking for a Senior Engineer to join our Agentic SOC team. At Eye, we organise engineering around streams: mission-driven groups with a clear outcome to drive, not a product area or a section of the codebase. This team's mission is to build LLM-powered agents that augment our security analysts, taking on repetitive investigation and triage work so humans can focus on the judgment-heavy parts of the job.

You will work in a small, full-stack team of 2 to 3 engineers contributing to your stream's goal, working across whatever systems and layers are needed to deliver it. This is a role for someone who wants real ownership, not a queue of tickets, and who is excited about shipping agents into a real production SOC where correctness, latency, and cost all matter.

In this role 

- Own features end-to-end as Feature Lead: scope the problem, coordinate work within your team, make day-to-day technical decisions, and ship it to production. You are trusted to take a high-level goal and turn it into a plan without close supervision.

- Lead the design and delivery of LLM agents that plug into our SOC workflows, including tool design, prompt and context engineering, evals, and guardrails. Make sound tradeoffs on accuracy, cost, latency, and how much autonomy to give the agent versus keeping a human in the loop.

- Drive technical design discussions in your stream and, where the work calls for it, influence architecture and standards beyond it. Set the bar for code quality, testing, and documentation on your team.

- Ground engineering decisions in outcomes. Push back when the "why" is unclear, propose simpler or faster paths to the business result, and stay close to the security analysts and customers your agents are meant to serve.

- Mentor engineers on your team and across the stream through pairing, code review, and design feedback. Act as a multiplier, not just a strong individual contributor.

- Participate in hiring: interview candidates, help shape the bar, and support onboarding.

- Contribute to a psychologically safe and outcome-oriented team culture. Lead by example in incidents and high-pressure moments.

- The role is remote in the Netherlands or in Berlin, with a commitment to travel to the office (The Hague or Berlin) twice per week.
